institution: Memory Injection Attacks on Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
subtitle: In collaboration with Dr. Shahnewaz Karim Sakib and Dr. Anindya Bijoy Das
highlights: Investigating existing memory injection attacks on LLM agents' long-term memory and their limitations.
Analyzing LLM agent memory vulnerabilities to improve both attack strategies and defense mechanisms.

institution: Proactive Security for Cross-Chain Bridges Against Adversarial Attacks
subtitle: In collaboration with Dr. Shahnewaz Karim Sakib and Dr. Anindya Bijoy Das

Identifying weaknesses in bridge architectures and developing proactive security mechanisms against them.

institution: Attack Scenarios in Cross-Chain Blockchain Interactions
subtitle: Supervised by Dr. Rahma Bintey Mufiz Mukta
highlights: Conducted a comprehensive survey and taxonomy of security vulnerabilities and attack patterns in cross-chain communication protocols.
Collected and analyzed 50+ real-world cross-chain bridge attack incidents from 2022 to August 2026, drawing from sources such as bridges' own post-mortem reports and third-party security audits.
Mapped attacks to specific attack patterns and functional domains based on analysis.

institution: Predictive Model for Birth Delivery Mode
subtitle: Supporting Dr. Rubana Hoque Chowdhury's PhD research

highlights.text: View my work for this research on GitHub:

highlights: Worked as a research assistant to Dr. Rubana Hoque Chowdhury on her PhD research in an iterative loop: reviewing the supplied literature, implementing the proposed methods in code, then jointly experimenting on and refining the resulting models.

Achieved 99% accuracy for cesarean vs. vaginal delivery prediction and 94% accuracy for spontaneous vs. induced delivery classification, using machine learning and geometric feature extraction on Electrohysterogram (EHG) signals.
Re-implemented and validated methods from prior published EHG studies, and built the analysis and figures behind two of her publications and her annual PhD committee reviews.
Supplied experimental evidence throughout her PhD journey, from proposal defence through dissertation submission and final defence.

institution: Bengali Keyword Extraction from Bengali Blogs (Transformer-Based Approach)
subtitle: Supervised by Dr. Muhammad Ibrahim Khan
highlights: Built a comprehensive Bengali blog dataset of 9,012 annotated posts.
Proposed a transformer-based dual-encoder architecture, achieving an 84% F1@10 score.
Ran a comparison analysis against existing keyword-extraction methods to benchmark the proposed approach.
